(12) Four Places Where Agents Stumble

Where the agent stumbles In the experiment
Composition Operations that work alone, but have to be chained Observed
Discovery The information exists, but the agent cannot get to it Observed
Semantics Words that mean more than the model assumes Partly observed
Errors Responses that derail the agent Observed

(21) The Creation Date Is in the OpenAPI Description 

# GitHub OpenAPI description (excerpt)
paths:
  /users/{username}:
    get:
      operationId: users/get-by-username
      summary: Get a user
      responses:
        "200":
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                oneOf:
                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/private-user"
                  - $ref: "#/components/schemas/public-user"
components:
  schemas:
    public-user:
      required: [login, id, ..., created_at, ...]
      properties:
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
  • github-openapi-get-user.yaml

(22) The MCP Tool Does Not Return It, and Does Not Say So 

# MCP tool definition (from tools/list, trimmed, shown as YAML)
name: search_users
description: >-
  Find GitHub users by username, real name, or other profile information.
  Useful for locating developers, contributors, or team members.
inputSchema:
  type: object
  properties:
    query:
      type: string
      description: >-
        User search query. Examples: 'john smith', 'location:seattle',
        'followers:>100'. Search is automatically scoped to type:user.
    sort:
      type: string
      description: >-
        Sort users by number of followers or repositories, or when the
        person joined GitHub.
      enum: [followers, repositories, joined]
  required: [query]
  • github-mcp-search-users.yaml

(24) Every Pull Request Is an Issue, and the Description Says So 

# GitHub OpenAPI description (excerpt)
paths:
  /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues:
    get:
      operationId: issues/list-for-repo
      summary: List repository issues
      description: |
        List issues in a repository. Only open issues will be listed.

        > [!NOTE]
        > GitHub's REST API considers every pull request an issue, but
        > not every issue is a pull request. For this reason, "Issues"
        > endpoints may return both issues and pull requests in the
        > response. You can identify pull requests by the `pull_request`
        > key. [...]

(27) A Trillion Operations for 16'968 ÷ 404?

CPU Computation LLM Inference
Elapsed time a few nanoseconds ~0.1–2 seconds
Computation one integer division ~1011–1013 FLOPs
Energy ~pJ–nJ ~1–100 J
Correctness exact not guaranteed
  • CPU: One deterministic instruction
  • LLM: Trillions of operations for probabilistic inference
  • The LLM might still get the answer wrong

(30) No Single Answer: Build a Toolbox

  • Where are you?
  • What kind of failures do you see?
  • How big is your landscape?
  • What should the next AI projects achieve?


Architect for Change Erik Wilde: What AI Agents Are Teaching Us About Integration

(31) Six Techniques, From Easy to Involved

Technique Effort
1 Check your APIs for AI readiness Easy
2 Improve the descriptions Easy, if automated
3 Improve the API designs More involved
4 Orchestrate tools into fewer, task-oriented tools More involved
5 Orchestrate deterministically (Arazzo or similar) More involved
6 Select or search the tools Different pattern

(34) What Agents Are Teaching Us

  • Integration problems did not go away. Agents meet them at runtime.
  • More tools can work, and cost more.
  • Watch agents to see what is missing.
  • As little AI as possible.
